title: China-to-Switzerland Solar PV Inverter Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Electromagnetic and Grid-Profile Evidence at 230/400 V 50 Hz
rows.target_requirement: Switzerland-facing inverters are typically assessed against IEC power-quality and EMC context where the 230/400 V, 50 Hz low-voltage profile is used with utility-specific settings. Even when frequency matches China, the nominal-voltage profile and project-specific harmonic, trip, and protection assumptions are part of the acceptance package.
target_standards: EN 50160 characteristics of public electricity supply
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese inverters are often defaulted against China 50 Hz grid evidence in GB/T 37408 and GB/T 19964, but same-frequency claims do not remove the need to map Swiss 230/400 V windows and protection assumptions for the exact model and project.
rows.gap: The gap is often project assumptions and evidence traceability. Exporters should provide Swiss settings tables, voltage/frequency and harmonic trip values, anti-islanding behavior, reconnection delays, documentation of EMC test scope, and commissioning evidence for each firmware version.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where project commissioning, utility review, or O&M requirements require proof of grid-profile and EMC settings.
mandatory_status.cn: Not equivalent — China 50 Hz profile reports must be mapped to Swiss 230/400 V and project requirements.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Even where frequency is matched, confirm Swiss 230/400 V settings, harmonic behavior, and project-specific protection and trip logic before energisation.

rows.target_requirement: Switzerland-facing solar inverters for grid use require project-level interconnection coordination with Swissgrid and local network operators. Approval typically covers connection documents, single-line diagrams, metering strategy, anti-islanding settings, reactive-power behavior, and commissioning evidence before energisation.
target_standards: ElCom electricity-market and network oversight framework
rows.china_equivalent: China grid procedures under GB/T 19964 and GB/T 37408 can support technical preparation, but project-level Swissgrid route and operator-specific commissioning requirements must be established independently for the destination site.
china_standards: China State Grid / China Southern Power Grid project procedures
rows.gap: The gap is the operational acceptance pack: utility project approval path, interface and relay settings, anti-islanding and LVRT/UVRT details, metering and telemetry readiness, and documented commissioning test acceptance for the selected Swiss connection point.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for project-level grid interconnection and commissioning under Swissgrid-relevant routes.
mandatory_status.cn: Not equivalent — China grid-connection procedures do not replace Swissgrid and local operator acceptance.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat Swissgrid interconnection as a separate project gate from product testing. Confirm operator-specific settings for the exact site and inverter configuration.

rows.requirement: TS EN 62109 Safety Evidence for PV Inverter Power Converters
rows.target_requirement: For Switzerland-facing PV inverters, TS EN 62109-1 and TS EN 62109-2 are commonly the relevant safety baseline for grid-connected power converters where SNV-adopted pathways or project requirements request it. Switzerland is not an EEA member, so conformity is handled through Swiss-adopted routes rather than direct EU-market legal status, and evidence should be mapped to the exact model and site conditions.
target_standards: SNV route under CE-aligned Swiss adoption where applicable
rows.china_equivalent: China baseline evidence may include GB/T 37408, GB/T 19964, and related performance or grid-connection reports. These are useful for engineering comparison but do not replace Switzerland-facing EN/IEC safety evidence in CE-aligned acceptance contexts.
rows.gap: The key gap is evidence scope and traceability: target model family, power ratings, thermal assumptions, isolation design, protection philosophy, voltage and frequency settings, commissioning logs, and multilingual labels and warnings for Switzerland.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where SNV-adopted EN/IEC safety evidence is requested by the project owner, distributor, network operator, or importer for Switzerland-facing interconnection.
mandatory_status.cn: Not equivalent — China GB/T safety evidence is China baseline only.

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] TS EN 62109 reporting helps close the technical gap only when mapped to Switzerland-facing project settings and commissioning scope, including 230/400 V and 50 Hz protections.
